name: GitLab.com
scope_notes: Group IP controls require Premium/Ultimate. Do not transfer Self-Managed 400-day/configuration options to GitLab.com.

controls.name: Require fine-grained personal access tokens after a specific date
controls.what: After the date, legacy PATs cannot access the top-level group, subgroups or projects; group/project/service-account tokens are exempt.
controls.setting: Top-level group > Settings > General > Permissions and group features
controls.quote: On GitLab.com, enforcement applies to the group and its subgroups and projects, and blocks legacy personal access tokens from accessing those resources after the enforcement date.

controls.name: Disable personal access tokens (enterprise users)
controls.what: Stops the group's enterprise users from creating PATs and disables their existing PATs; service account PATs unaffected.
controls.setting: Group > Settings > General > Permissions and group features > Enterprise users
controls.quote: Stops the enterprise users from creating new personal access tokens. This behavior applies even if an enterprise user is also an administrator of the group. Disables the existing personal access tokens of the enterprise users.

controls.name: Users can create group access tokens and project access tokens in this group
controls.what: Clearing it blocks new group/project access tokens across the group; existing ones stay valid.
controls.setting: Top-level group > Settings > General > Permissions and group features
controls.quote: The restriction covers the entire group, including all subgroups and their projects. Existing tokens remain valid until they expire or you revoke them.

controls.name: Restrict access by IP address
controls.what: Limits UI and API access to the group to listed CIDRs, including group/project tokens, deploy keys and CI clone operations.
controls.setting: Top-level group > Settings > General > Permissions and group features
controls.quote: IP restrictions apply to project and group access tokens, service accounts, deploy keys, and deploy tokens.

controls.name: Enforce SSO-only authentication for Git and Dependency Proxy activity
controls.what: Git over HTTPS/SSH and Git-related API calls by users need an active SSO session; not enforced for bot tokens or CI jobs.
controls.quote: For Git activity over SSH and HTTPS, users must have at least one active session signed-in through SSO before they can push to or pull from a GitLab repository.

controls.name: Credentials inventory (revoke tokens)
controls.what: Top-level group owners view and revoke enterprise users' PATs and group/project access tokens.
controls.quote: On GitLab.com, the credentials inventory monitors enterprise users and service accounts in a top-level group.

controls.name: CI/CD job token allowlist
controls.what: Only jobs from the project itself and allowlisted groups/projects can use a job token against this project.
controls.setting: Project > Settings > CI/CD > Job token permissions
controls.quote: By default, job token access is restricted to only CI/CD jobs that run in pipelines in your project.

controls.name: Fine-grained permissions for job tokens
controls.what: Limits allowlisted job tokens to a set of REST API endpoints.
controls.setting: Project > Settings > CI/CD > Job token permissions (allowlist entry)
controls.quote: You can use fine-grained permissions to explicitly allow access to a limited set of REST API endpoints.

controls.name: Allow Git push requests to the repository
controls.what: Off by default; when off job tokens cannot push to the repository.
controls.setting: Project > Settings > CI/CD > Job token permissions; projects API
controls.quote: You can configure your project to allow Git push requests that are authenticated with a CI/CD job token. This setting is turned off by default.

controls.name: Limit job token scope for public or internal projects (feature visibility)
controls.what: Setting features to 'Only project members' stops non-allowlisted job tokens reading artifacts, registries, releases or the repo.
controls.setting: Project > Settings > General > Visibility, project features, permissions
controls.quote: You can limit access to these actions to only the projects on the allowlist by setting each feature to be only visible to project members.

no_control.what: Group SSO enforcement does not apply to API requests (PAT or OAuth).
no_control.quote: SSO enforcement does not apply to API requests. However, you can disable password and passkey authentication for enterprise users to prevent password-based API access.

no_control.what: Web SSO enforcement does not cover project/group access tokens, service accounts or deploy keys.
no_control.quote: Credentials that are not tied to regular users (for example, project and group access tokens, service accounts, and deploy keys) do not have the SSO check enforced.

no_control.what: Fine-grained token enforcement does not cover service account, group or project access tokens.
no_control.quote: Enforcement does not apply to tokens for service accounts, group access tokens, or project access tokens.

no_control.what: Group IP restrictions do not cover runner registration or job requests.
no_control.quote: IP restrictions do not apply to runner registration or when runners request or update CI/CD jobs.

containment.steps: DELETE /personal_access_tokens/:id (or self); DELETE /projects/:id/access_tokens/:token_id or groups equivalent; or revoke in UI. Admins can revoke any user's PAT; Self-Managed admins can identify a leaked value via POST /admin/token.
